title: Checkout
summary: A shopping cart with discount codes, totals in whole cents and a printable receipt.

tasks.title: Adding an item twice
brief: Customers say that tapping “Add to basket” a second time leaves the quantity unchanged, and sometimes lowers it. Adding 2 teas then 1 more tea leaves 1 tea.
Find the cause, fix it and add a regression test.
done: Adding a SKU already in the cart adds to its quantity.
The cart still has one line per SKU, so the receipt shows a single combined row.

questions: If the same SKU is added with a different price, which wins? (Out of scope; keep the first price, but mention it.)
Should the merged line stay in its original position on the receipt? (Yes.)
orient: README rule: “adding a SKU that is already in the cart increases its quantity”.
Searched for “qty” to find every place quantity changes: only Cart.add writes it.
Baseline: all tests pass; none add the same SKU twice.
trace: Cart.add finds the existing line, then assigns qty instead of adding to it.
wrapUp: Cause: the merge branch in Cart.add replaced the quantity rather than increasing it.
Fix: `existing.qty += qty`, plus a regression test.
Noticed but not changed: a repeat add with a different unit price silently keeps the old price. Worth a product decision.

tasks.title: Shipping and grand total
brief: Add shipping. Orders under $50.00 after discounts pay a flat $4.99; orders of $50.00 or more ship free. An empty cart has no shipping.
Add Cart.shipping() and Cart.grandTotal() (total plus shipping). Leave total() as it is, because the payments team reads it.
done: shipping() is 499 for non-empty carts under 5000 cents after discount, else 0.
grandTotal() is total() + shipping(); total() is unchanged.

questions: Is the $50 threshold before or after discount? (After.)
Should the receipt show shipping? (Not in this task; note it.)
orient: All amounts are integer cents; matched that with named constants SHIPPING_CENTS and FREE_SHIPPING_FROM.
total() already applies the discount and floors at zero, so shipping builds on it.
trace: Checked the edge cases on paper: empty cart, exactly 5000, and a discount that drops a 5200 cart to 4680.
wrapUp: Added shipping() and grandTotal() on top of total(), with the two numbers as named constants.
With more time: add a shipping row to the receipt, and move pricing rules into one module.
